passage:
In social studies class, students learned that countries sometimes make agreements to protect parts of the ocean beyond national borders.
The teacher explained that no single country owns all oceans, but many countries use them. Fishing, shipping, mining, and pollution can affect shared waters.
Students played a negotiation game. Each group represented a country with different needs. They quickly found that protecting shared resources was difficult.
If one group took too much, others suffered. If no one trusted each other, the agreement failed.
The game made international cooperation feel real. A shared ocean needs shared rules, or everyone loses.
